newsitem.title: THAILAND: Laotian power project faces two-year delay.
newsitem.headline: Laotian power project faces two-year delay.

text.p: Laos' 681-megawatt Nam Theun 2 hydro power project faced an additional two-year delay and it would not come on stream until 2002, a member of the project's financing consortium said on Wednesday.

Implementation of the $1.1 billion project has been delayed pending an environmental impact assessment, which would help the World Bank determine whether to guarantee loans for consortium members, as well as for the bank to extend its own $100 million loan.
Adisai Bodharamik, Chairman of Jasmine International Plc, which holds a stake of about 10 percent in the consortium, said he was convinced the delayed project would be completed.
"I think the project is good and it will go ahead but we might not be able to bring it to capacity on time. I think it could be put back one and half, or two years," he said.
The project, earlier scheduled to come on stream by 2000, is part of a plan for the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) to buy power from neighbouring Laos.
Other consortium members were Electricite de France, Australia's Transfield Construction-Asia, Thailand's Phatra Thanakit Plc, and Italian-Thai Development Plc.
Resource-poor Laos is currently implementing several other hydro-power schemes which will produce electricity for sales to to power hungry neighbours like Thailand.
